metadata.summary: If the International Team are going to end Team USA’s Presidents Cup dominance this week, live on Sky Sports, they may require their own 'Miracle at Medinah' to do it.
metadata.content: Presidents Cup 2026: Can Europe inspire new 'Miracle at Medinah' and shock International Team victory over Team USA? | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Presidents Cup 2026: Can Europe inspire new 'Miracle at Medinah' and shock International Team victory over Team USA? Team USA have won the last 10 editions of the Presidents Cup; Geoff Ogilvy captains the International Team as they look for a first victory on American soil; Ryan Fox revealed how the Internationals plan to take inspiration from Team Europe this week at Medinah, live on Sky Sports Golf Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Tuesday 22 September 2026 16:11, UK Image: Adam Scott, Ryan Fox, Hideki Matsuyama and Min Woo Lee all feature for the International Team at the Presidents Cup If the International Team are going to end Team USA’s Presidents Cup dominance this week, live on Sky Sports, they may require their own 'Miracle at Medinah' to do it. Fourteen years on from Team Europe producing a historic final-day comeback to claim Ryder Cup glory at the same venue, Geoff Ogilvy sees his side head in as heavy underdogs to avoid an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup defeat. The United States have won every edition since 2005 and only been beaten once in the event's history, before seven of the 24 players involved in this year's contest were even born, with all logic pointing to that run continuing in Illinois. messages.text: Dual Champion Hurdle winner Hurricane Fly dies aged 22

metadata.summary: Hurricane Fly, the Willie Mullins-trained dual Champion Hurdle winner, has died at the age of 22.
metadata.content: Hurricane Fly: Willie Mullins-trained dual Champion Hurdle winner dies aged 22 | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Hurricane Fly: Willie Mullins-trained dual Champion Hurdle winner dies aged 22 Willie Mullins' brilliant hurdler Hurricane Fly has passed away at the age of 22; the winner of 22 Grade 1's will be remembered as one of the all-time greats of the National Hunt sphere. Tuesday 22 September 2026 18:23, UK Image: Hurricane Fly ridden by Ruby Walsh jumps the last fence and goes on to win the Stan James Champion Hurdle Challenge Trophy Hurricane Fly, the Willie Mullins-trained dual Champion Hurdle winner, has died at the age of 22. The son of Montjeu proved himself one of the greats of recent National Hunt history, winning the Champion Hurdle at Cheltenham in 2011 and 2013 and the Irish Champion Hurdle five times on the spin between 2011 and 2015. In total Hurricane Fly won a record breaking 22 Grade One races. He was retired in 2015 after a nine-year career to spend his days alongside other equine greats such as Faugheen, Hardy Eustace and Beef Or Salmon at the Irish National Stud. Mullins described the superstar hurdler as "awesome" and "one of the biggest legends" to pass through his Closutton yard. Regular jockey Ruby Walsh simply labelled him "the perfect horse" and the best jumper of a hurdle he ever rode.
